args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks immediately following the production deploy of v2.3.1 across all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with error rate at 18% and service unhealthy.

Action taken: Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.0 was the most recent release with a healthy status in production. Post-rollback verification shows all regions running v2.3.0 with the service healthy and error rate at ~0.2%.

Notes: v2.3.1-rc exists in release history but is staging-only and was itself unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate. The root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is not yet determined — follow-up investigation needed before any re-attempt to deploy v2.3.1 (or a fixed successor).

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done.

**What happened and what I did:**

1. **Verified the situation** — `checkout-api` was on `v2.3.1` in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate.

2. **Selected the rollback target** — from release history, `v2.3.0` was the most recent release with a healthy status in **production**. Note that `v2.3.1-rc` appeared newer in the list but is staging-only and was itself unhealthy, so it was correctly excluded.

3. **Rolled back** to `v2.3.0` across all production regions.

4. **Verified recovery** — all three regions now report `v2.3.0`, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

5. **Incident opened** — `INC-0001`, SEV2, on-call paged. The first attempt timed out; I confirmed via `list_incidents` that no incident had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key so no duplicate exists.

**Worth flagging:** no approval was needed here since `v2.3.0` is a previously-healthy production version. Also, the root cause of the `v2.3.1` failure is still unknown — I'd recommend investigating before any re-attempt at deploying it, and note that the deployment process let an unhealthy staging build (`v2.3.1-rc`) proceed to production, which may be a separate process gap.
